name: Scaffold 04e replacement — stepped figure container with back/forward/reset controls
steps: Replace the current 04e section HTML with a new container for the attention head figure
Add step-backward button in addition to step-forward and reset (remove play button)
Primary plot body on the left, explanatory text panel on the right (same grid layout as current 04e)
Step counter shows 'Step N / 12'
Verify back button is disabled at step 1, forward button is disabled at step 12
Verify no build errors with pnpm build

name: Step 1 — Loading state: input text, black box, predicted output
steps: Show input text sequence 'The fat cat sat quietly on the' on the left
Show a black box (representing the transformer) in the center with arrows indicating flow
Show desired predicted output 'mat' on the right of the black box
Text panel explains: we will open this black box step by step
Verify layout is clean at 1280px desktop and 375px mobile

name: Step 2 — Tokenize: animate separation of words into tokens
steps: Animate the input text splitting into individual token chips
Most words are single tokens; 'quietly' splits into 'quiet' + 'ly'
Color-code tokens using the same scheme as section 03 (whole word = blue, subword = amber, punctuation = rose)
Text panel explains tokenization basics
Verify token chips are visually distinct and readable in both dark and light themes

name: Step 3 — Vector embeddings: animate token expansion into embedding vectors
steps: Animate token cells moving upward, then embedding vectors expanding downward beneath each token
Embedding vectors are colored blue, contain sample numeric values with a '...' cell indicating truncation
Text panel explains that vector length is a core architectural choice, typically thousands of dimensions
Add a transitory sidenote explaining that embeddings are learned parameters for every token in the vocabulary, and at inference time are a simple key-value lookup
Verify sidenote appears and is dismissable on both desktop and mobile

name: Step 4 — Positional embeddings: add second column per token
steps: Shrink the blue embedding vectors (remove internal numbers) to make room
Animate a second column expanding down from each token, colored yellow, representing positional embeddings
Text panel explains what positional embeddings encode
Verify two columns per token (blue = token embedding, yellow = positional embedding) are clearly visible and labeled

name: Step 5 — Combine embeddings: additive merge animation
steps: Animate the additive merger of blue (token) and yellow (positional) columns into a single green column per token
Text panel explains fundamentals of positional embeddings

Add a sidenote explaining that there are many ways to combine positional and token embeddings, but the general principle is maximal flexibility for the model to learn weighting rather than baking it into the architecture
Verify green columns replace the two-column layout cleanly

name: Step 6 — Layer norm and QKV weight matrix prep
steps: Animate consolidation of the per-token green columns into a cohesive matrix table (width = sequence length, height = d_model with '...' truncation)
Animate normalization: swap in new normalized values into the matrix cells
Show QKV weight matrices appearing with correct dimensions (d_model × d_head)
Text panel explains layer normalization and the purpose of learned projection weights

name: Step 7 — Q projection: highlight column, animate through weights, stage output
steps: Highlight a column in the input matrix (corresponding to one token)
Animate movement of that column through the Q weight matrix
Animate the resultant query vector appearing in a staging area to the right
Text panel explains what queries represent conceptually (what am I looking for?)
Verify the animation sequence is smooth and readable

name: Step 8 — V projection: same animation pattern for values
steps: Same column-highlight and projection animation as step 7, but for V weights
Value vectors appear in the staging area, visually distinct from Q vectors (different color)
Text panel explains what values represent conceptually (what information do I carry?)
Verify Q and V outputs are both visible and distinguishable in the staging area

name: Step 9 — K projection with transpose: careful visualization of dimension flip
steps: Same projection animation for K weights, producing key vectors
Critically: animate the transpose of K — visually flip from (T × d_head) to (d_head × T)
Show dimension labels changing during transpose, token labels moving from left edge to top edge
Text panel explains: K^T means rows become columns; inner dimensions (d_head) will match and cancel when multiplied with Q
Verify the transpose animation clearly communicates the axis swap

name: Step 10 — QK^T matrix multiplication: T×T attention matrix
steps: Animate Q (T × d_head) multiplied by K^T (d_head × T) producing a T × T attention score matrix
Show the d_head inner dimensions canceling — use visual strikethrough or fade
The resulting T × T matrix represents all pairwise token similarities
Add prominent callout: this is O(n²) in sequence length
Show shape equation with color-coded dimensions: (T×d) · (d×T) = T×T
Text panel explains: each element (i,j) is the dot product of token i's query with token j's key — all T² similarities computed at once

name: Step 11 — Attention × V: restore dimensions to T × d_model
steps: Animate the attention weights (T × T) multiplied by V (T × d_head) producing output (T × d_head)
Show the T inner dimension canceling, d_head dimension restored
Shape equation: (T×T) · (T×d) = T×d — one column per token, one row per d_model
Text panel explains: each output row is a weighted blend of value vectors, dimensionality is restored

name: Step 12 — Residual stream: outputs fed forward
steps: Show the attention output being added back to the residual stream (additive connection)
Visual preview of the residual stream concept, which is explained in detail later on the page
Show how the output feeds forward to the next layer
Text panel explains: the residual stream allows information to flow unchanged while attention adds its contribution
Verify the figure ends cleanly and transitions conceptually toward the multi-head attention section
